checkout-to-marketplace.briefing:
What’s going on
Challenge: Checkout → marketplace.
Diagram involves: Order, Payment, Razorpay, Database.

Evolve simple checkout into marketplace stages.

The problem (simple terms)
Something about this design makes the next product change expensive, confusing, or unsafe. Your job is to understand that pressure and improve the design carefully.

What you should do
Read the diagram before changing anything. Prefer focused edits over a full rewrite. Preserve behavior that should still work.

evo-multi-provider.title: Evolve to Multi-Provider Payments
evo-multi-provider.description: Year-1 single provider → multi-provider without breaking Order. A short evolution track.
evo-multi-provider.briefing:
What’s going on
Year 1 supports a single payment provider. Evolve so more providers can be added without breaking Order.

stageTitles.title: Single provider OK
stageTitles.requirement: Only Razorpay exists. No second provider yet. Hold is fine.

stageTitles.title: Add Stripe
stageTitles.requirement: Stripe must be supported beside Razorpay. Order must not depend on concrete providers.

evo-food-delivery.title: Food Delivery Platform
evo-food-delivery.description: Start from a simple food-delivery MVP and evolve it through growth, payments, async notifications, regions, and reliability — including stages where holding is correct.
evo-food-delivery.briefing:
What’s going on
You are the architect for a food-delivery startup. Day 0 is intentionally simple: Customer → OrderService → Restaurant / PaymentService / Database.

The journey
Over ~a year the business will add users, payment providers, async messaging, multi-region restaurants, and a hard availability target.

The rule
Evolve the existing design. Do not wipe and redraw. Sometimes the right move is to hold.

stageTitles.title: MVP launch
stageTitles.requirement:
You launch with a handful of restaurants in one city. Customers place orders; restaurants accept; payments charge cards; everything persists to one database.

Traffic is low. Latency is fine. The team is three engineers.

Look at the baseline. Does anything need to change for launch day?

stageTitles.title: 10K daily orders
stageTitles.requirement:
Orders are up to ~10,000/day. Peak dinner hours feel a bit slower, but p95 is still under 300ms and error rates are fine.

Leadership asks “should we microservices this?”

Decide whether the current architecture still works.

stageTitles.title: Payment bottleneck
stageTitles.requirement:
Daily orders hit ~1M. PaymentService is now the bottleneck — synchronous charge calls stretch p95 past 2s at peak.

Users abandon carts. Finance also wants a second provider next quarter.

This time, holding is unlikely to be enough.

stageTitles.title: Multiple payment providers
stageTitles.requirement:
Finance signed Razorpay beside Stripe. Checkout must support both. OrderService should not grow provider if/else forever.

If you deferred the payment abstraction earlier, that debt is due now.

stageTitles.title: Notification delays
stageTitles.requirement:
Incident: email/SMS sends are blocking order completion. Support tickets spike when the email vendor slows down.

Notifications must not block the order happy path.

stageTitles.title: Multi-region restaurants
stageTitles.requirement:
Restaurants now operate in five countries. Latency to a single region DB hurts. Local payment methods differ. A full region outage must not take down every market.

Availability target moves toward 99.99%.

evo-parking-lot.title: Parking Lot Over Years
evo-parking-lot.description: Evolve a parking lot from a single floor through EV charging, reservations, and dynamic pricing — product growth without premature scale theater.
evo-parking-lot.briefing:
What’s going on
Year-by-year product evolution of a parking system. Start simple. Add floors, EV, reservations, then pricing — only when the story demands it.

stageTitles.title: Single lot MVP
stageTitles.requirement: One lot, cars and bikes, park/unpark/fee. City council just approved the lot. No multi-floor requirement yet.

stageTitles.title: Multiple floors
stageTitles.requirement: The building adds floors. Spots must be tracked per floor. Fee rules still exist, but inventory is now multi-level.

stageTitles.title: EV charging
stageTitles.requirement: EV spots with chargers arrive. Not every spot is EV. Charging sessions must be modeled without breaking normal park/unpark.

stageTitles.title: Reservations
stageTitles.requirement: Users can reserve spots ahead of time. Holds expire. Walk-ins still work.

stageTitles.title: Dynamic pricing
stageTitles.requirement: Pricing now varies by hour, floor, and EV. Fee logic should not live forever inside ParkingLot.

evo-ride-share.title: Ride-Share Matching Growth
evo-ride-share.description: Grow a ride-share matcher from city MVP through surge pricing to multi-city — scale and geo pressures.
evo-ride-share.briefing:
What’s going on
A ride-share MVP matches riders to drivers in one city. Grow carefully through surge and multi-city expansion.

stageTitles.title: City MVP
stageTitles.requirement: One city, simple matching. Hold unless you see a real pressure.

stageTitles.title: Surge pricing
stageTitles.requirement: Peak hours need surge multipliers. Pricing policy should not tangle forever inside MatchingService.

stageTitles.title: Multi-city
stageTitles.requirement: Launch in 12 cities. Matching must be city-scoped. A city outage must not freeze the whole network.

evo-payments-growth.title: Payments Under Fire
evo-payments-growth.description: Single PSP → multi-provider → timeout incident → audit. Business + incident pressures on payments.
evo-payments-growth.briefing:
What’s going on
Payments start glued to Stripe. Grow providers, survive an outage, then satisfy audit.

stageTitles.title: Add second PSP
stageTitles.requirement: Razorpay is signed. Stripe must keep working. Prefer a gateway so Order stays clean.

stageTitles.title: Provider outage 15 minutes
stageTitles.requirement: Production incident: primary PSP unavailable for 15 minutes. Checkout failed hard. How should architecture reduce blast radius next time?

stageTitles.title: Audit every payment
stageTitles.requirement: Compliance needs an audit trail for charge and refund across providers — one choke point, not copy-paste in each adapter.

evo-notifications.title: Notifications Under Load
evo-notifications.description: Sync email → multi-channel → backlog incident → async. Product + incident pressures.
evo-notifications.briefing:
What’s going on
Notifications start as a synchronous email send after order complete. Evolve channels and isolate failures.

stageTitles.title: Add SMS + WhatsApp
stageTitles.requirement: Support wants SMS and WhatsApp beside email. Prefer a channel abstraction.

stageTitles.title: Vendor backlog incident
stageTitles.requirement: Email vendor queues for 40 minutes. Order completion waits on notify(). Checkout looks “down”.

evo-team-boundaries.title: Team Topology Pressure
evo-team-boundaries.description: A monolith owned by 3 engineers becomes painful when 8 teams need independent delivery. Architecture must respect ownership boundaries.
evo-team-boundaries.briefing:
What’s going on
Architecture is also about how teams work. Watch org growth force module boundaries — not because of runtime TPS, but because of ownership.

stageTitles.title: Three engineers
stageTitles.requirement: Three engineers own everything. Shared DB and monolith are fine. Don’t invent platforms yet.

stageTitles.title: Eight teams
stageTitles.requirement:
Eight teams now ship independently. Deploying auth blocks checkout. SharedDatabase becomes a conflict magnet.

Architecture must introduce clearer ownership boundaries / modules / APIs — not necessarily a full microservice zoo.

evo-legacy-checkout.title: Legacy Checkout Untangle
evo-legacy-checkout.description: Inherit a tangled checkout. Grow traffic while gradually untangling — legacy evolution under scale pressure.
evo-legacy-checkout.briefing:
What’s going on
You inherit a god CheckoutController. You cannot rewrite everything on day one. Evolve under increasing load — sometimes hold, sometimes extract.

stageTitles.title: Inherit the mess
stageTitles.requirement: Traffic is modest. The code is ugly but paying the bills. A full rewrite is riskier than living with it short-term.

stageTitles.title: Payment extraction
stageTitles.requirement: Fraud team needs cleaner payment hooks. Extract payment without boiling the ocean.

stageTitles.title: Traffic 20×
stageTitles.requirement: Orders 20×. Synchronous email and fat controller become visible latency. Deferred email debt may be due.
